rules.description: Test files must use environment variables or dynamic values for secrets, not hardcoded strings
rules.message: Test secrets must use os.environ.get() / process.env or dynamic generators — hardcoded secrets in tests get committed to version control

rules.description: Avoid using eval()
rules.message: eval() is dangerous - use safer alternatives

rules.description: Avoid Function constructor for dynamic code
rules.message: Function constructor can execute arbitrary code - use safer alternatives

rules.description: Avoid string concatenation in SQL queries (excludes parser/generator files)
rules.design_check: Does the design use ORM or parameterized queries for all database interactions? Flag any mention of string-concatenated SQL. BLOCK.
rules.message: SQL injection risk - use parameterized queries

rules.description: Avoid raw SQL with user input
rules.message: Potential SQL injection - use parameterized queries

rules.description: Avoid shell command with user input
rules.message: Command injection risk - sanitize input or use safer alternatives

rules.description: Avoid Python shell execution with user input
rules.message: Command injection risk - use subprocess with list arguments and shell=False

rules.description: Avoid innerHTML with user input
rules.design_check: Does the frontend design use innerHTML with dynamic user content? Replace with textContent or a sanitization library. Flag.
rules.message: XSS risk - use textContent or sanitize HTML

rules.description: Avoid outerHTML with user input
rules.message: XSS risk - use textContent or sanitize HTML

rules.description: Avoid document.write for dynamic content
rules.message: XSS risk - document.write can execute scripts from user input

rules.description: Avoid React dangerouslySetInnerHTML
rules.message: XSS risk - ensure HTML is sanitized with DOMPurify or similar

rules.description: Avoid path concatenation with user input
rules.message: Path traversal risk - validate and sanitize file paths from user input

rules.description: Detect potential path traversal patterns
rules.message: Path traversal pattern detected - ensure proper path validation

rules.description: Password requirements should be enforced
rules.message: Password minimum length should be at least 8 characters

rules.description: Passwords should be hashed, not stored in plain text
rules.design_check: Does the design specify password hashing using bcrypt or argon2? Reject any design that stores passwords in plaintext or using reversible encryption. BLOCK.
rules.message: Ensure passwords are hashed before storage (use bcrypt)

rules.description: Session cookies should be secure
rules.design_check: Does the session design specify secure: true, httpOnly: true, sameSite settings for cookies? Flag if session configuration is underspecified.
rules.message: Session cookies should have secure: true in production

rules.description: Authentication checks should not have bypass conditions
rules.design_check: Does the design have any authentication bypass conditions (e.g., skipAuth flag, admin=true from client)? BLOCK on any bypass mechanism.
rules.message: Review authentication bypass logic for security

rules.description: Avoid CORS wildcard in production
rules.design_check: Does the API design specify CORS configuration? Ensure specific origins are whitelisted, not wildcard (*). Flag wildcard CORS.
rules.message: CORS wildcard (*) should not be used in production

rules.description: Enable CSRF protection for state-changing operations
rules.design_check: Does the API design include CSRF protection for state-changing operations (POST/PUT/DELETE)? Flag if CSRF middleware is not mentioned.
rules.message: Ensure CSRF protection is enabled for POST/PUT/DELETE routes

rules.description: Do not log sensitive information
rules.design_check: Does the logging design expose sensitive fields (auth tokens, API keys, secrets, passwords)? Remove them. BLOCK.
rules.message: Do not log sensitive information like passwords or tokens

rules.description: Do not expose stack traces in responses
rules.design_check: Does the error handling design return stack traces to clients? Stack traces must be logged internally only, not returned in API responses. BLOCK.
rules.message: Do not expose stack traces to clients

rules.description: Avoid weak cryptographic algorithms
rules.design_check: Does the design use MD5 or SHA1 for any security-sensitive hashing? Replace with SHA-256+ or bcrypt/argon2 for passwords. BLOCK.
rules.message: Use stronger hash algorithms (SHA-256 or better)

rules.description: Do not use hardcoded initialization vectors
rules.message: IV should be randomly generated, not hardcoded

rules.description: Do not trust role from client input
rules.design_check: Does the design accept role or permission values from client requests (req.body.role, req.body.isAdmin)? Roles must come from the authentication token or database, never from client input. BLOCK.
rules.message: Never trust role/permission from client input

rules.description: Block cloud metadata IPs
rules.message: Block access to cloud metadata endpoints

rules.description: Block executable uploads
rules.design_check: Does the file upload design restrict allowed file types? Ensure executable formats (.exe, .sh, .bat, .js, .php) are blocked. BLOCK if no type restriction is specified.
rules.message: Executable files must not be allowed for upload

rules.description: Avoid unsafe deserialization
rules.message: Unsafe deserialization detected - use safe formats and validation

rules.description: Containers must not run privileged
rules.message: Privileged containers are not allowed

security_anti_patterns.description: Common security mistakes and what NOT to do - learn from real-world failures

rules.description: NEVER trust client-side validation alone
rules.design_check: Does the design rely only on client-side validation for security-sensitive operations? Server-side validation is mandatory for all inputs. BLOCK.
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Client-side validation is for UX only. ALWAYS validate on the server. Attackers bypass client-side validation trivially.

examples.bad: // Client validates email format, server trusts it
examples.good: // Server re-validates all input regardless of client validation

rules.description: NEVER rely on security by obscurity
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Security by obscurity fails. Use proper authentication and authorization. URLs are logged, cached, and leaked.

rules.description: NEVER implement custom cryptography
rules.design_check: Does the design propose custom cryptographic implementations? Use established libraries (bcrypt, argon2, libsodium). BLOCK on custom crypto.
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Never roll your own crypto. Use established libraries (bcrypt, argon2, libsodium). Custom crypto has subtle vulnerabilities.

rules.description: NEVER store passwords in plaintext or reversible encryption
rules.design_check: Does the design store passwords in plaintext or using reversible encryption? Only one-way hashing (bcrypt/argon2) is acceptable. BLOCK.
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Never encrypt passwords (encryption is reversible). Use one-way hashing with bcrypt or argon2.

rules.description: NEVER use MD5 or SHA1 for password hashing
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: MD5 and SHA1 are broken for passwords. Use bcrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2 with high cost factor.

rules.description: NEVER compare passwords with == or ===
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Direct password comparison exposes timing attacks. Use constant-time comparison (crypto.timingSafeEqual).

rules.description: NEVER expose stack traces to users in production
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Stack traces expose internal paths, versions, and logic. Log internally, return generic message to users.

rules.description: NEVER expose raw database errors to users
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Database errors reveal schema, table names, and query structure. Log internally, return generic message.

rules.description: NEVER hardcode secrets in source code
rules.design_check: Does the design reference any secrets inline? All secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens) must come from environment variables or a secrets manager. BLOCK.
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Hardcoded secrets end up in version control. Use environment variables or secret managers.
rules.mitigation: Use process.env.SECRET_NAME or a secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault)

rules.description: NEVER disable SSL certificate verification
rules.design_check: Does the design disable SSL certificate verification anywhere? BLOCK — fix certificate issues properly, never disable verification.
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Disabling SSL verification enables man-in-the-middle attacks. Fix certificate issues properly.

rules.description: NEVER use HTTP for sensitive data transmission
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: HTTP transmits data in plaintext. Always use HTTPS for anything sensitive.

rules.description: NEVER store JWTs in localStorage for authentication
rules.design_check: Does the frontend design store JWT tokens in localStorage? Use httpOnly cookies instead to prevent XSS token theft. BLOCK.
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: localStorage is vulnerable to XSS. Use httpOnly cookies for auth tokens.

rules.description: NEVER use long-lived access tokens without refresh mechanism
rules.design_check: Does the design use long-lived access tokens (days/weeks) without a refresh mechanism? Use short-lived access tokens + refresh tokens. Flag if token expiry is not specified.
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Long-lived tokens increase attack window. Use short-lived access tokens with refresh tokens.

rules.description: NEVER combine CORS wildcard with credentials
rules.design_check: Does the design combine wildcard CORS origin with credentials: true? This is forbidden. Use specific allowed origins. BLOCK.
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Wildcard CORS with credentials is dangerous. Explicitly whitelist allowed origins.

rules.description: NEVER directly assign request body to database models
rules.design_check: Does the design pass request body directly to database create/update operations? Whitelist allowed fields explicitly. BLOCK.
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Mass assignment allows attackers to set unintended fields (isAdmin, role). Whitelist allowed fields.

rules.description: AVOID exposing sequential IDs for enumerable resources
rules.design_check: Does the design expose sequential integer IDs for user-facing resources? Use UUIDs to prevent enumeration attacks. Flag for review.
rules.message: CAUTION: Sequential IDs allow enumeration attacks. Consider UUIDs for user-facing resources and always enforce authorization.

rules.description: NEVER enable debug mode in production
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Debug mode exposes sensitive information and may allow code execution. Disable in production.

rules.description: NEVER catch all errors and ignore them
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Silent error handling hides security issues. Log errors, then handle or rethrow appropriately.
